title: Calcutta
era_role: Apertura dell'EP Two (luglio 2017, Basick Records). Abbandona il pastoralismo inglese di One per una trilogia di titoli legati a città storiche/antiche (Calcutta, Nazareth, Jericho). Rappresenta la brama fisica e spirituale ('Until I wake I dine on old encounters').

in_character_quotes.quote: He is everywhere, at all times. Vessel encountered Sleep in a dream, with promise of glory and magnificence if Vessel followed Him. The UK is old, decaying and rich in folklore.
in_character_quotes.source_title: Metal Hammer / Louder - Who and what the hell are Sleep Token? (pubblicata per il lancio di Calcutta)

editorial_reading.summary: Presentato in anteprima su Metal Hammer nel maggio 2017, il brano accompagna la prima vera intervista in-character del gruppo e introduce il video girato in ambienti boschivi e rituali.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - Who and what the hell are Sleep Token

editorial_reading.summary: The anonymous collective known as Sleep Token are premiering their new video for Calcutta exclusively with Metal Hammer. Taken from their upcoming EP Two, it’s an odd and unique mix of technical metal and expansive indie soundscapes. But that’s not the only bizarre thing going on…

editorial_reading.summary: The song Calcutta is a bizarre mix of mainstream anthemic indie and tech-metal. What on earth is going on there?
editorial_reading.source_title: Metal Hammer / Louder - Who and what the hell are Sleep Token? (2017)

editorial_reading.summary: OK, so their ‘backstory’ is silly. But as far as the music’s concerned, Sleep Token are an undeniably intriguing prospect, inhibiting a sparse world of heart-breaking beauty and intense heaviness where stark, and sometimes sinister, skeletal soundscapes build to throbbing climaxes with mesmerising effect. Recent single Calcutta, which premiered on Hammer’s website, builds like a storm: violent, djent-tinged destruction erupting amid Vessel’s ethereal and vulnerable Bon Iver-esque vocals.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - Sleep Token: goofy gimmick or serious art?

editorial_reading.summary: A big part of that is their unique, boundary-crossing sound. Mixing R&B, metalcore and tech metal elements, Sleep Token sit somewhere outside the usual metal scene spheres whilst appealing to fans of all of them - and even beyond. With three albums, two EPs and a bunch of stand-alone songs fleshing out their mysterious lore, we figured it high time to dive deep into the world of Sleep Token and decipher some of the possible meanings behind their songs. Tin-foil hats on folks: we're going deep.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song (Page 1)

editorial_reading.summary: The three songs on Sleep Token’s second EP are named after historical settlements, each one older than the last – seemingly a metaphor for the decay of a relationship. Calcutta is named after the British-Indian settlement that was established in the late 17th Century, though the region has been inhabited for more than 2,000 years.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song (Page 1)

editorial_reading.summary: The song sees Vessel sounding repaired by a new partner (or maybe Sleep). ‘Missing pieces find me,’ he intones at one point, later adding, ‘You are more than warm belief / Melting skywards / More than silence broken / I’m whole again.’ Spoiler alert: it won’t last.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song (Page 1)

editorial_reading.summary: “Mine” shows the inescapable nature of the relationship Vessel has found himself in, through teleological lines such as “we are a crashing course driven by a holy force.” The word ‘tangled’ is used repeatedly throughout Sleep Token’s discography (“Calcutta”, “The Night Does Not Belong To God”, “Say That You Will”, “Blood Sport”, “Chokehold”) to reiterate the inescapability of the situation. It is obsessive. The song could represent Sleep’s desire, sounding big and sweet and romantic, while truthfully being deliberately manipulative. The end repeats the lyrics to a far darker musical accompaniment – the beginning of the relationship is positive, mutually beneficial, and at the end there’s no escape and the rot has set in. Then it returns to the peaceful rendition. On the one hand, it could be interpreted as the narrator losing faith in the statement and trying to convince themselves, or as a typical response to trauma; rather than fight a situation they can’t see any way out of, people often simply let the waves take them under. Nautical metaphors are littered throughout TPWBYT.
editorial_reading.source_title: Boolin Tunes - The Lore of Sleep Token

editorial_reading.summary: Thanks to Scarlett Heselwood for their suggested chronological placement of “Calcutta” and “Nazareth”.

editorial_reading.summary: Sleep Token are an anonymous English rock band formed in London in 2016. They have released four studio albums, two EPs, two standalone songs, and multiple covers.

In May 2017, it was announced that Sleep Token had signed with independent label Basick Records and would release their second EP Two in July.[5] Ahead of the EP's release, the group issued two new singles – "Calcutta" in May and "Nazareth" in June.[6][7] "Calcutta" received an exclusive premiere through Metal Hammer, where writer Luke Morton described the song as "an odd and unique mix of technical metal and expansive indie soundscapes".[8]

In the 2017 Metal Hammer interview, Vessel revealed that the "markings on his mask" were the band's initials in "ancient runes".[8] He is referring to his original mask, which can be seen in the videos for "Calcutta" and "Nazareth."

community_theories.theory: Sleep Token’s logo has remained one of the band’s greatest unsolved mysteries ever since it first appeared on the physical release of their debut EP One in 2016. With only 50 copies ever made, however, most fans likely encountered the symbol for the first time on the cover of their 2017 single Hey Ya!. The logo later took on a new life in the music video for Calcutta, where it appeared painted in red across II’s mask. Its geometric design has sparked endless speculation, with fans linking it to everything from alchemical symbols to ancient alphabets like runes. Yet the mystery only deepened in 2019, when the logo changed, making it even more difficult to find a theory that explains both versions.
community_theories.source_title: Lore of Sleep Token - Logo & Early Symbols

community_theories.theory: The EP consist of 3 songs Calcutta, Nazareth, and Jericho. Before releasing the EP, the band had already released both Calcutta and Nazareth as singles on May 5th and June 19th, 2017 respectively.

Sleep Token are an anonymous masked collective band formed in London in 2016. The band is well-known for their genre-bending style of music. They worship the ancient deity called Sleep. "We are here to serve Sleep and project His message." is what Vessel answered when asked to talk about the band's lore. Vessel encountered Sleep in a dream, Sleep promised him glory and magnificence if he follows Sleep.[1] Each song created is a "Token" (an offering) to the deity known as Sleep. Since 2016, the band has released two EPs, four studio albums, two standalone singles, and multiple covers.
Calcutta is the first track and first single from Sleep Token's second EP, Two. Calcutta released on May 5th, 2017, while it's music video would be released on May 20th, 2017.
The song's title is named after the capital city Calcutta, which is located in the Indian state of West Bengal, which is known officially as Kolkata today.[1]

Calcutta's single art, and essentially Two's cover art, originates from a design for a traditionally constructed Hindu temple in the 12th-century Hoysala dynasty style, which was created by Adam Hardy from Cardiff University.[2][3]
